key_insight: Deep learning models trained on large-scale functional assays can discover and de novo design internal ribosome entry sites (IRES) that program RNA translation, enabling predictable control of protein expression from RNA. The approach closes a design–build–test loop to produce novel, experimentally validated IRES sequences.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between slow, low-throughput experimental IRES discovery and the vast combinatorial RNA sequence space by enabling scalable, data-driven discovery and engineering of translation-regulating elements.
method: Generate high-throughput sequence-to-function data by assaying thousands of candidate IRES sequences for translation activity.
Train deep learning sequence-to-function models (predictors and interpretable components) to map RNA sequence/structure to translational output.
Use model-guided generative design and optimization to create de novo IRES with targeted translation profiles and validate candidates experimentally.
impact: Demonstrates a reusable AI-driven blueprint for biological sequence design: ML models + high-throughput assays enable controllable, interpretable generation of functional biomolecules, accelerating therapeutic RNA design and sequence engineering research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: high-throughput assay → model training → generative design → experimental validation (closed loop).
Predicted vs measured activity scatterplot or bar chart showing model accuracy and validated de novo IRES performance.
Sequence logos / attention maps highlighting learned motifs and structure features correlated with translation.
Schematic showing tunable translation levels enabled by designed IRES (icons for low/medium/high expression).
paper_title: Programmable RNA translation through deep learning-driven IRES discovery and de novo generation
paper_authors: Yanyi Chu, Di Yin, Dan Yu, Guangxue Xu, Junze Zhang
